messages:
alex: Quick sync — we need to lock the telemetry contract for continuous-batching metrics. Console panels + rollout UX depend on consistent names/labels. Meeting tomorrow 11am PT but wanted to get a short async thread first. Key asks: canonical metric names, label set (model/deployment/route), sampling, and whether runtime emits per-batcher or aggregated per-node.
maria: +1. Core metrics I care about: batch_size_histogram, batch_wait_ms (p50/p95), in_flight_batches, batch_fill_rate, node_saturation_pct. Labels: model, deployment, route, quantization_profile, region. Keep batcher_id optional for debug.
vikram: For routing/policy visibility we also need per-route dropped_due_to_quota and dropped_due_to_capacity. Those feed into autoscaler and quota alerts. Suggest labels: route, customer_tier.
tara: Console/rollout UX notes: panels should default to a 5m rolling window and allow compare-by-deployment (canary vs prod). Rollout checks should flag significant shifts in batch_size distribution or median wait_time during canary. Proposal: auto-annotate rollout timeline when batch p50 changes > 15% for 10m.
alex: Important: cardinality concerns. If we add route + deployment + model + quantization_profile that's a lot. Propose: primary low-cardinality view (model, deployment, route) and a debug high-cardinality stream gated by a debug flag that includes batcher_id and host_id.
maria: Agreed on two-tier approach. Also propose we export a summarized histogram for batch sizes: explicit buckets that map to our UX: [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128]. That gives a compact shape without per-batch labels.
vikram: Telemetry format note: runtime currently emits an envelope: 
```json
{"metric": "redwood.batch.wait_ms", "value": 12.4, "labels": {"model":"gpt-4r", "deployment":"dedicated-a", "route":"/generate", "bucket":"8"}}
```
We should standardize envelope and batching behaviour (emit both histogram bucket increments and summary p50/p95 every Ns).
 tara: UX-wise the rollout page needs both raw histogram and a computed "batch-shape-score" (0-100) so product can show if batching got worse after a change. Thresholds: > 30 score => block rollout. We can tune.
 alex: runtime/infra inputs — runtime should emit: batch_size_histogram, batch_wait_ms_summary (p50/p95), in_flight_batches, fill_rate, saturation_pct. Infra should add node-level capacity and device_utilization metrics so console can compute cluster-level saturation.
maria: Implementation detail: for Prometheus/ingest we recommend metric names: 
- redwood_batch_size_bucket{le,model,deployment,route,region}
- redwood_batch_wait_ms_summary{quantile,model,deployment,route,region}
- redwood_in_flight_batches{model,deployment,route,region}
- redwood_batch_fill_rate{model,deployment,route,region}
- redwood_node_saturation_pct{node_id,device_type,region}
Keep snake_case and prefix with redwood_.
vikram: +1 on naming, but for node_id label we must guard cardinality. node_id only for infra debug; use node_pool label for normal dashboards.
 alex: A couple of small API debates: 1) Should runtime export p50/p95 or should the telemetry pipeline calculate quantiles? 2) Histogram buckets vs Exponential summary.
maria: My vote: runtime should emit bucket increments and counts; pipeline computes rolling quantiles. That keeps runtime cheap and pipeline flexible.
vikram: If we do that, add an occasional summary emit (every 30s) to help low-latency dashboards.
tara: For rollout automation, we need a stable signal: use pipeline-computed p50/p95 with a smoothing window (1m) and an immediate anomaly signal from the runtime short-summary.
deploy-bot: metric redwood.batch.wait_ms_summary registered in telemetry pipeline (ingest-id: t-48c9) :rocket:
sre-bot: Added a runbook checklist stub for batch saturation alerts and rollout interactions: https://redwood.internal/wiki/runbooks/batch-sat-checklist :white_check_mark:
alex: Action items captured: 1) vikram — PR with envelope/schema + sampling rules by EOD. 2) maria — dashboard proto (mock panels + queries) by Wed. 3) tara — rollout gating proposal (thresholds + auto-annotate rules) by Thu. 4) infra — add node_pool and device_utilization exports (owners: ops infra) this week. Everyone please ack.
maria: ack
vikram: ack
tara: ack
sre-bot: ack (added owners to runbook)
alex: Thanks all — will spin up the 11am PT sync to walk through the dashboard proto and finalize cardinality tradeoffs.
